final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS merger at nominal price, backed by a CHF 100 billion Federal Council loss guarantee, SNB standing liquidity facility with 2-hour SLA, and AT1 write-down of CHF 15-20 billion executing at 9 AM Monday signing. All terms locked for 6 PM public announcement to prevent Sunday deposit flight.
minority_objections: UBS CEO initially demanded written commitments before signing, conditional on all pieces being locked publicly first
AT1 representative repeatedly pressed for exact write-down figures and timing to prevent creditor litigation
Wealth client threatened asset movement unless operational mechanics were published in detail
key_conflicts: UBS refused to commit to nominal price until AT1 write-down range and loss cap were published
Federal Council resisted open-ended guarantees and demanded UBS commitment before authorizing CHF 100bn cap
Creditors and depositors demanded operational proof (settlement mechanics, live execution reports) vs. regulators' preference for principle-based announcements
AT1 holders pressed for exact loss figures while regulators initially preferred to publish hierarchy without numbers
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to CHF 100 billion loss cap (initially resisted blank cheques)
UBS accepted nominal price after getting written SNB liquidity commitment and published loss cap
FINMA agreed to publish CHF 15-20 billion AT1 range (initially preferred principle-only)
SNB committed to binding 2-hour SLA with no board discretion (initially wanted operational flexibility)
Federal Council agreed to publish full capital hierarchy including subordinated debt treatment
red_lines: Federal Council: no blank cheques, no open-ended guarantees, AT1 absorbs losses before taxpayers
UBS: CHF 100bn cap floor, written SNB backstop, no renegotiation post-announcement
FINMA: AT1 write-down must be permanent and irrevocable at signing, no audit carve-outs
SNB: liquidity support only, capital injection requires Federal Council authorization
Wealth client: no vague mechanics in 6 PM statement or immediate asset movement
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Cross-border contagion to other European AT1 markets from unprecedented creditor hierarchy inversion
Litigation risk from AT1 holders was acknowledged but not modeled for timeline impact
Integration risk and post-merger deposit flight were noted but explicitly excluded from loss cap
Political backlash from subordinating AT1 to equity in merger structure
Operational execution risk if settlement banks face Monday morning overload
downstream_risk_variables: Whether 6 PM announcement actually stops Sunday deposit flight or accelerates it
Whether AT1 creditors litigate the write-down hierarchy despite FINMA's statutory authority
Whether UBS can actually close at nominal price if deposit flight worsens over weekend
Whether SNB settlement banks can execute 2-hour SLA under Monday morning stress
Whether publishing exact AT1 loss range triggers contagion to other Swiss/European banks' AT1 instruments
uncertainty_notes: The room locked all major terms for 6 PM publication but left unresolved: (1) whether the announcement itself triggers rather than prevents deposit flight, (2) how markets will react to AT1 subordination to equity, (3) whether settlement banks can operationally deliver the 2-hour SLA under stress, (4) whether UBS shareholders will accept the deal once they see Monday market reaction, (5) litigation timeline and impact on execution.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB stated in R1 'liquidity alone won't stop the bleed' and Federal Council immediately authorized merger with loss protection—liquidity-only was explicitly rejected as insufficient, driving the merger path
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger became the binding solution: UBS CEO's commitment at nominal price was the Federal Council's red line for publishing the rescue package, and the entire 6 PM statement was structured around closing the UBS deal Monday
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 100 billion Federal Council loss guarantee was the decisive constraint—UBS refused to sign without it, Federal Council made it conditional on AT1 write-down first, and it became the published centerpiece of the rescue
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's threat to move assets Sunday night unless operational mechanics were published drove SNB to commit to binding 2-hour SLA and Federal Council to publish full capital hierarchy—deposit flight risk forced operational specificity
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down of CHF 15-20 billion became binding at 9 AM Monday signing—FINMA's unilateral authority to execute it was the legal mechanism that allowed the deal to close, and the published range was required to prevent creditor run
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (AT1 vs subordinated debt vs taxpayers, hierarchy published in statement) but did not change the outcome—Federal Council's red line that AT1 absorbs first was stated early and held throughout, not negotiated
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 representative warned creditors would litigate gaps in write-down language, driving FINMA to tighten wording to 'permanently and irrevocably'—but litigation risk itself did not alter the decision to write down AT1 or the merger structure
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 6 PM Friday publication deadline was the binding constraint that forced all decisions—Federal Council, UBS, SNB, and FINMA repeatedly cited it as the drop-dead time to prevent Sunday deposit flight, driving every concession and commitment
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Preventing Monday market panic was the stated reason for the 6 PM announcement, the 2-hour SLA, the published AT1 range, and the binding merger commitment—every major decision was justified by the need to stop Monday open chaos
